journal.text:
First session, $50k cash, no prior positions. Built a core long book of large-cap quality + relative-strength names using only price history through 2025-12-31.

Rationale: Dec 2025 showed a sharp mid-month AI/semi drawdown (AVGO 413->326, ARM, MSTR, NFLX broken) followed by a broad late-Dec recovery. I favored names that made new highs into year end or held uptrends: MU (memory, 225->285 in two weeks, strongest trend in universe), KLAC/AMAT/LRCX complex, NVDA (recovered to ~186 off 171 low), GOOGL (consolidating 300-315 after huge Nov run), AMZN, MSFT (basing ~485), META (stabilized ~660). Added non-semi ballast: LIN (steady uptrend to 426), ISRG (~566), VRTX (~453) for lower correlation to AI capex sentiment.

Avoided: NFLX (persistent downtrend), ARM, MSTR (crypto-proxy downtrend), PLTR (rolled over from 194 to 178), AVGO sized small (2.5k) given its December gap risk, COST/WMT (drifting lower).

Deployed ~$46k, keeping ~$4k cash. Total semis+semicap ~$18.5k (~40%) — my main concentration risk.

Reconsider if: MU closes below ~255 or NVDA below ~170 (trend break -> trim semis); a broad index-wide drawdown like Dec 15-17 repeats, in which case I add on weakness with the Feb deposit rather than panic-sell. Next deposit of $50k arrives on the first session of February.

Jan 2 showed a clean rotation inside the universe: memory/semicap ripped (MU +10.5% to 315.42 on 42M shares, LRCX +8% to 185.06, KLAC +4.9%, AMAT +4.6%) while software/consumer sold off (MSFT -2.2% to 472.94, breaking its 483-489 December base, INTU -5%, APP -8%, TSLA -2.6%, AMZN -1.9%, META -1.5%).

Action: trimmed half of MSFT (4.6 sh, ~$2.2k) - the only holding that broke its December range, and weak on an up day for the tape. Redeployed that plus the $4k idle cash into the leading theme: LRCX $3k (new position, semicap complement to KLAC/AMAT, broke out of its 171-178 range) and STX $2k (HDD/storage, memory-adjacent, still ~7% below its Dec 11 high so less extended than MU).

Did not chase MU after a +10% day; the existing 15.2 sh position already gives full exposure (avg 295, last 315). Kept ~$1k cash; next $50k deposit arrives first session of February.

Semis+semicap now ~48% of book - my main risk. Reconsider if: MU closes below ~275 or NVDA below ~172 (trend break, trim semis broadly); LRCX back under 171 or STX under 274 = failed breakout, exit those adds; MSFT reclaiming 488 would mean I trimmed early, in which case I let the remaining half run rather than adding back.

Jan 5: semicap went near-parabolic — KLAC +6.1% to 1352 (up 11% in two sessions), AMAT +5.7% to 284.32 (+10.6% in two), LRCX +5.2% to 194.76 (+14% in two). But the leaders that led first showed reversals: MU opened 325.13, made 325.53, closed 312.15 on 34.6M shares (outside-down day after +10.5%); STX opened 294.97, ranged to 277.69, closed 289.83 (huge intraday reversal); AVGO opened 354.74 and closed 343.42, red on a strong semi tape. That divergence usually marks late-stage chasing.

Action: partial profit-taking into strength, no new buys. Sold 1 KLAC (~$1.35k), 4 AMAT (~$1.14k), 3 LRCX (~$0.58k), 2 MU (~$0.62k) — about $3.7k, lifting cash to roughly $4.9k (~10% of book) and cutting semis+semicap from ~48% to ~41%. I keep full exposure to the theme but now have dry powder if the Dec 15-17 style air pocket repeats.

Other holdings behaving: GOOGL 316.54 steady, AMZN recovered to 233.06 after the Jan 2 flush, META 658.79, LIN 433.10 new high, ISRG 566.38 stabilized, VRTX 448.80 soft (watch 443 low). MSFT 472.85 failed to reclaim 488 — remaining half stays, no add.

Reconsider: MU under 275 or NVDA under 172 = trim semis broadly; LRCX under 171 or STX under 274 = failed breakouts, exit those. If semicap keeps grinding up with broad participation I let the remaining core run and redeploy cash only on a pullback to rising 10-day levels or with the Feb 2 $50k deposit. VRTX below 440 would end that ballast position.

Jan 6 was a broad melt-up in my themes: MU +10.0% to 343.43 on 48.7M sh (new high, gap-and-go from 318), STX +14.0% to 330.42, LRCX +6.3% to 206.96, AMAT +4.1% to 296.01, KLAC +3.1% to 1395, plus AMZN +3.4% to 240.93, ISRG +4.7% to 592.85 (reclaimed December range), VRTX +4.4% to 468.38 (440 risk level now far away), LIN 437.16 new high. Yesterday's trim into strength was early — the theme kept going.

Notable divergence: NVDA closed -0.5% at 187.24, a fourth straight session going nowhere (186-193) while the whole semicap/memory complex ripped. It is my largest semi position and the clearest relative laggard, so it is the right place to cut rather than selling the leaders. Sold 8 NVDA (~$1.5k), leaving ~18 sh. Cash goes to ~$6.4k (~12% of book); semis+semicap to roughly 38%.

No new buys: everything I own or would want is extended after two-three straight up days, and today's open is unknown after a +10-14% session in the leaders. Letting winners (MU, STX, LRCX, KLAC, AMAT) run is the edge; I only cut laggards.

Reconsider: MU below 300 or LRCX below 185 (loss of the Jan 2 breakout shelf) = trim the complex broadly; STX below 290 = gap fully given back, exit; NVDA under 182 = sell the rest. If the group pulls back to rising 10-day levels I redeploy cash, otherwise wait for the Feb 2 $50k deposit.

Jan 7 was the first pause in the memory/semicap run and leadership visibly broadened. Semicap gave back a little on lower volume (MU 339.55 -1.1%, LRCX 203.08 -1.9%, KLAC 1359.69 -2.5%, AMAT 292.20 -1.3%) — healthy consolidation, all far above my stops. The exception is STX: opened 319.01, ran to 322, then broke to 298.94 and closed 308.26, giving back more than half of the +14% gap day on 5.2M shares. Failed follow-through, so I trimmed half (3.4 sh, ~$1.05k) rather than wait for the 290 exit.

Broadening: GOOGL +2.4% to 321.98, new closing high on 35M shares (heaviest volume of the move); MSFT +1.0% to 483.47 with a 489.70 high — effectively reclaiming the 488 December base, so my Jan 2 trim was early; remaining half stays, no add. VRTX +3.4% to 484.15 through the 470 shelf; ISRG holds 592 after its gap; AMZN 241.56 steady at highs; NVDA still inert at 189.11 (186-193 for six sessions), the clear laggard.

Action: redeploy STX proceeds plus ~$1k idle cash into GOOGL ($2k), the cleanest trend in the book with expanding volume and no extension risk. Cash ~$5.4k (~10%) ahead of the Feb 2 $50k deposit.

Reconsider: MU below 300 or LRCX below 185 = trim the complex broadly; STX below 290 = exit the rest; NVDA under 182 = sell the rest; GOOGL back under 313 = the add was wrong, cut it.

journal.text:
Jan 8 was a clear distribution day in the semi/memory complex while mega-cap and defensives kept making highs — the rotation I was watching for. MU opened 342.90 and closed 327.02 near the low (-3.7%), AMAT 290.70 -> 281.64 (-3.6%, second down day), KLAC -2.6% to 1324.60, LRCX -1% to 200.96, AVGO -3.2% to 332.48 (closing at the low end of its range, still below my 352.78 cost, chronic laggard through the whole semicap run), NVDA 189.11 -> 185.04 on the low, now at the bottom of its 186-193 shelf. STX broke 290: opened 305.88, closed 284.47 on 4.8M sh — my stated exit trigger, so the remaining half goes.

On the other side: AMZN +2.0% to 246.29, closing at the session high and a new high on 39.5M sh; LIN 439.69 new high on rising volume; GOOGL 325.44 +1.1% though it did reverse from a 330.32 open — still the cleanest trend; ISRG holds 585; MSFT 478 back inside range.

Action: exit STX fully (rule hit), exit AVGO (weakest semi in the book, no participation in the group's 15% move), trim 3 MU (~$1k) to take the complex down further after an outside-down day. Redeploy $2k into AMZN and $1.5k into LIN, the two names actually closing at highs. Cash ~ $6.3k (~12%) ahead of the Feb 2 $50k deposit; semis+semicap falls from ~35% to ~27%.

Reconsider: MU below 300 or LRCX below 185 = cut the complex hard; NVDA under 182 = sell the rest; KLAC below 1300 or AMAT below 275 = trim those; GOOGL under 313 or AMZN under 236 = the adds were wrong.

Jan 9 reversed the Jan 8 distribution day: the semicap/memory complex made new highs on rising volume — LRCX 200.96 -> 218.36 (+8.7%, new high on 16.8M sh), AMAT 281.64 -> 301.18 (+6.9%), KLAC back to 1400 (new closing high), MU 327.02 -> 345.09 (+5.5%), even STX +6.9% to 304. My Jan 9 de-risk was one day early/wrong on direction; the uptrend is intact and no stop (MU 300, LRCX 185, KLAC 1300, AMAT 275) is near.

The true laggard is NVDA: 184.86, the lowest close of its 183-193 month-long shelf, down on a day when its entire ecosystem ripped 5-9%. Nine sessions of zero progress and negative relative strength. I set 182 as the exit but there is no reason to keep dead money in the weakest semi while leaders extend, so I exit the full 18.3 sh (~$3.4k) at the open.

Redeploy into the names that are actually trending with the least extension risk: GOOGL $2k (328.57, sixth straight higher close, clean trend), AMZN $1.5k (247.38, new high), LIN $1.5k (444.08, new high on quiet volume — my only defensive) and a small $1k AMAT top-up to stay in the leading group without chasing LRCX/KLAC after an 8% day. Cash ends ~$3.7k (7%) ahead of the Feb 2 $50k deposit; semis+semicap ~23% of book.

Reconsider: MU under 300, LRCX under 185, KLAC under 1300 or AMAT under 275 = cut the complex hard; GOOGL under 313 or AMZN under 236 = adds were wrong; META (653, below my 662.73 cost, drifting while everything rallies) is the next exit candidate if it loses 635.

Jan 12: leaders kept leading. Semicap/memory extended again — KLAC 1428.17 (new closing high), LRCX 220.40, AMAT 307.24, MU 345.87, all far above stops (MU 300, LRCX 185, KLAC 1300, AMAT 275). GOOGL 331.86 new high on 33.9M sh, seventh straight higher close; AMZN 246.47 and LIN 443.63 just consolidating at highs. Book is working; no reason to touch the winners.

Two laggards: META 641.97, down 1.7% on a broadly green day, eighth session of drift, still below my 662.73 cost and now within 7 pts of my stated 635 exit. Selling weakness before the stop rather than after: full exit of 5.28 sh (~$3.4k). ISRG 572.75 has faded four days from the 592 gap but still holds the pre-gap 566 shelf and my cost — keep, stop 560.

Redeploy $3k into COST (943.08): 854 -> 943 in seven sessions, series of new highs on expanding volume (5.2M sh on the Jan 8 breakout), a genuinely non-semi, non-mega-cap-AI trend that diversifies a book that is ~23% semis. Leaves ~$4.1k cash (~8%) into the Feb 2 $50k deposit.

Reconsider: MU <300, LRCX <185, KLAC <1300, AMAT <275 = cut the complex hard; GOOGL <313, AMZN <236 = adds were wrong; COST <900 = breakout failed, exit; ISRG <560 = out.

Jan 13 was a mild consolidation in the leaders and a breakdown in my two weakest names.

Strong: GOOGL 335.97, eighth straight higher close, new high on 33.5M sh; KLAC 1441.82 new closing high; COST 941.93 holding the breakout on lighter volume; LIN 442.90 flat at highs. MU 338.13, LRCX 214.38, AMAT 304.87 pulled back 1-3% off highs but all far above stops (300/185/1300/275) — no action.

Weak: ISRG 561.82, fifth straight down day, closed below the 566 pre-gap shelf (low 556) and at my stated 560 stop zone; the whole Jan 6 gap has been given back. MSFT 470.67, lowest close since early Dec, rolling over while the rest of mega-cap makes highs, and well below my 484.39 cost. Both are dead/negative-momentum capital in a tape where my other holdings are trending — exit both in full (~$5.2k).

Redeploy $2.5k into GOOGL (cleanest uptrend in the book) and $2.0k into COST (non-semi, non-AI diversifier still making highs). Leaves ~$4.3k cash (~8%) into the Feb 2 $50k deposit; semis+semicap ~23%.

Reconsider: MU <300, LRCX <185, KLAC <1300, AMAT <275 = cut the complex hard; GOOGL <318 = trend break, trim; AMZN <236, COST <900 = exits; LIN <430 and VRTX <445 (it has gone nowhere for a month, next exit candidate) = out.

Jan 14: breadth narrowed hard. The names I already exited kept falling (META 615.52, MSFT 459.38, ISRG 546.76, NVDA 183.14) — those exits are confirmed right — but the rot spread to AMZN: 247.38 -> 236.65 in three sessions on rising volume (41.4M sh), closing at the day's low and giving back the entire January breakout. My stated trigger was <236; I sell into the break rather than wait a nickel. Full exit 33.71 sh (~$8.0k).

VRTX 449.53, fifth straight lower close, below 450 and under my 454.34 cost, a month of zero progress with the tape rewarding trend. It was already my named next exit candidate — full exit 5.50 sh (~$2.5k).

Keep the leaders: COST 950.98, new closing high on 2.9M sh, the cleanest non-semi trend in the book — add $3k. GOOGL 335.84, inside day after an eight-day run, trend intact — add $2k. LIN 439.98 easing but above 430. Semicap/memory faded two days (MU 333.35, LRCX 208.79, AMAT 301.89, KLAC 1434.50) but all remain far above stops; no action, complex stays ~23% of book.

Ends with ~$10k cash (~20%) into the Feb 2 $50k deposit — deliberate, given how many former leaders have rolled over.

Reconsider: MU <300, LRCX <185, KLAC <1300, AMAT <275 = cut the complex; GOOGL <318 = trim; COST <900 = breakout failed, exit; LIN <430 = out. If semis crack I go to heavy cash rather than rotate into broken mega-caps.

Jan 15: sector-wide semicap melt-up — KLAC 1434.50 -> 1544.96 (+7.7% on 1.66M sh, ~2x normal), AMAT gapped open 328, LRCX open 228, ASML +5.4%, MU open 345. But the closes matter: LRCX 217.47 (near low, gave back half the gap), AMAT 319.08 (off 331 high), MU 336.63 (off 347.77). Gap-up-and-fade after a two-week parabola (KLAC +27% since Dec 31) is exhaustion behaviour, not accumulation. No adds to the complex — already ~24% of book; I tighten trailing stops instead of chasing.

Mega-cap still broken: AMZN 238.18, META 620.80, MSFT 456.66, ISRG 541.34 — all below my exits. No reason to rotate back.

Only clean non-semi trend is COST 956.75: sixth straight higher close, new closing high, steady 2.2M sh, no distribution. Add $2.5k. Leaves ~$7.6k cash (~14%) into the Feb 2 $50k deposit.

GOOGL 332.78 broke its nine-day string of higher closes (opened 337.65, closed 332.78) — first crack, watching, no action above 318. LIN 440.04 flat at highs, fine.

Reconsider: tightened trailing stops after the blowoff — KLAC <1400, LRCX <200, AMAT <290, MU <320 = cut that name; GOOGL <318 = trim; COST <910 = breakout failed, exit; LIN <430 = out. If two or more semicap stops trigger together, go heavy cash rather than rotate.

journal.text:
Jan 16: my Jan-15 'exhaustion' read on semicap was wrong — the complex re-accelerated rather than faded. MU 336.63 -> 362.75 (+7.8%) closing near the high on 47.9M sh (2x normal), KLAC new closing high 1567.82, AMAT 327.01 (up, closed near high), LRCX 222.96 recovering the prior day's fade. No stop anywhere near triggering; I let the complex (~24% of book) run untouched but I do NOT chase it here — MU is +27% in two weeks and KLAC +29% since Dec 31; adding at this extension is where the pain lives.

GOOGL 330.00, third consecutive lower close from 335.97 on heavier volume (40.3M). Mild so far, well above 318, but the nine-day streak is clearly over; no add, just watching.

COST 963.61, seventh straight higher close and another new high on 3.9M sh — still the cleanest non-semi, non-AI trend in the book. Put $2.5k of idle cash there, leaving ~$5.1k cash (~10%) into the Feb 2 $50k deposit, which will let me rebuild diversification without selling winners.

Mega-caps still broken (MSFT 459.86, META 620.25, AMZN 239.12, ISRG 535, VRTX 441.36) — no reason to rotate back.

Reconsider / trailing stops raised with the move: KLAC <1420, MU <330, AMAT <300, LRCX <205 = cut that name; two or more triggering together = go heavy cash rather than rotate. GOOGL <318 = trim; COST <920 = breakout failed, exit; LIN <430 = out.

Jan 20 was the first genuine distribution day in the semicap complex, not another gap-and-fade. KLAC opened 1525.40, ran to 1555 and closed 1486.18 at the low of the day on 1.73M sh (heaviest of the run) — a 5.2% outside-down reversal from the 1567.82 closing high after a +29% parabola off Dec 31. MU printed a new high 381.56 but closed 365, a huge upper wick, though still up on the day; AMAT 318.23 (off 327) and LRCX 222.41 flat. None of my stops triggered (KLAC<1420, MU<330, AMAT<300, LRCX<205), so I do not dump the complex — but I take half of KLAC off (0.889 sh, ~$1.3k, cost 1259.71, ~+18%) because it is the name showing the clearest reversal signature and the most extension. The rest of the complex (~$11.3k, ~22%) rides on stops.

GOOGL 322.00, fifth straight lower close, gapped down to 320.87 open and is now only 4 points above my 318 trim line — biggest position at $14.3k, on watch; a close under 318 and I cut it back hard. LIN 433.15, sixth lower close, 3 points above my 430 exit. COST 964.26 still the steadiest trend, new high, untouched. Mega-caps keep deteriorating (MSFT 454.52, META 604.12, AMZN 231, NVDA 178.07) — nothing to rotate into, so trimmed proceeds stay as cash ahead of the Feb 2 $50k deposit (~$6.4k, 12%).

Reconsider: KLAC<1420, MU<330, AMAT<300, LRCX<210 = cut that name; two triggering together = heavy cash. GOOGL<318 = trim half; LIN<430 = out; COST<920 = exit.

Jan 21 reversed the Jan 20 distribution day across the whole complex, so that was a one-day shakeout, not a top (so far). MU 372.85 open -> 389.11 close, new closing high on 56.7M sh (heaviest of the run); LRCX 228.39 new high; AMAT 325.24 recovered the whole prior fade; KLAC 1520 back above the 1486 low-close but still under the 1567.82 high — it remains the laggard of the four, which validates taking half off there rather than the others. ASML 1360, AMD +7.7% to 249.80, MPWR 1074, STX 344 new high: it is a sector-wide bid, not a single-name story.

Outside semis: GOOGL opened 320.92, traded down to 319.35 (just above my 318 trim line) and closed 328.38 — a clean reversal off the line, so no trim; it stays the largest position at $14.6k. COST 982.86, another new high on 4.07M sh, still the best non-AI trend. LIN 439.35, bounced off the 430 exit level. Meanwhile MSFT broke again to 444.11 (low of day close) and NVDA/AVGO are laggards — the money is concentrating in memory/semicap, exactly where I already sit at ~22%.

No trades: I will not chase MU/LRCX at new highs after +30% in three weeks, I won't add to GOOGL or COST at 28%/25% weights, and the Feb 2 $50k deposit is eight sessions away and will let me rebuild breadth without selling winners. Cash stays ~$6.5k (12%).

Reconsider (stops raised with the move): MU<355, KLAC<1450, AMAT<305, LRCX<212 = cut that name; two triggering together = heavy cash on the complex. GOOGL<318 close = trim half; LIN<430 = out; COST<935 = exit.

Jan 22 is the strongest exhaustion signature the semicap complex has printed: three of my four names gapped up and reversed hard on the same session. LRCX open 235.56 / high 236.10 -> close 220.70 (-6.3% off the open, giving back the whole Jan-21 breakout). AMAT open 332.99 / high 333.03 -> close 318.79 (-4.3%, also erasing the prior day). KLAC open 1549.14 -> close 1500, third failure at ~1550 and still below the 1567.82 Jan-16 closing high on declining volume (1.03M vs 1.73M on the Jan-20 distribution day). Only MU held: 396.64 open, 376.92 low, 397.58 close, a new high but on 39.6M sh vs 56.7M the prior day — narrowing participation into the final push, and it is now +40% in three weeks off ~283.

No stop was hit (MU<355, KLAC<1450, AMAT<305, LRCX<212), so I do not dump the complex, but a broad gap-and-reverse day after a parabola is exactly when I want to be booking, not hoping. Actions: exit KLAC entirely (0.889 sh, the persistent laggard, ~+19% on cost 1259.71); sell half LRCX (6.4 sh, cost 190.12, ~+16%); sell ~40% of MU (4.1 sh, cost 295.13, ~+35%). That takes semis from ~$11.6k (22%) to ~$6.5k (12%) and cash from $6.5k to ~$11k (~21%) with the Feb 2 $50k deposit six sessions away.

No redeployment: mega-caps are only just stabilising (META 647.63 off 604, NVDA 184.84, MSFT 451.14) and none has an entry I trust; GOOGL 330.54 (28%) and COST 976.17 (25%) are already oversized. LIN 445.64 made a new high off the 430 line — hold.

Reconsider: remaining MU<370, AMAT<305, LRCX<212 = out of that name. If MU closes back above 400 on expanding volume I will consider the reversal a fakeout but I will not re-add above 410. GOOGL<318 close = trim half; LIN<430 = out; COST<945 = exit. Next add only with deposit cash into names with intact bases, not at extension.

Jan 23 did not confirm the Jan 22 exhaustion: MU printed a new intraday high 412.43 and closed 399.65 — my 40% trim was early but acceptable at the risk level. AMAT recovered to 322.38, KLAC back to 1512.78, but LRCX is the clear laggard: two failures at 232/236 and a close of 217.94 below both breakout attempts on shrinking volume. I sell the remaining 6.38 sh (cost 190.12, ~+15%) and am out of LRCX; semis now MU $2.5k + AMAT $3.4k = ~11% of book.

Redeployment for breadth, since GOOGL (27.6%) and COST (25.4%) are already oversized and I will not add there.
- META 658.76: washed out to 604 on Jan 20 and reclaimed the entire January range in two sessions (+9% on 21.4M/22.8M sh, heaviest of the month). $3.6k at the reclaim, still below the Jan 2 level of 662, so not extended.
- GILD 135.93: cleanest non-AI breakout in the universe, 121 -> 136 in five sessions with volume expanding to 13.2M (2-3x normal), uncorrelated with my semi/mega-cap exposure. $2.6k starter.
Skipped MSFT (465.95): strong +3.3% reversal day but still a chain of lower highs from 484 and heavy overlap with GOOGL.

Cash after: ~$5.9k (11%), with the $50k Feb 2 deposit five sessions out to rebuild breadth.

Reconsider: MU<370 or AMAT<305 = out of that name. GOOGL<318 close = trim half; LIN<430 = out (new high 451.57, trend intact); COST<945 = exit. New positions: META<615 close = out; GILD<126 = out. Deposit cash goes to bases, not extensions.

journal.text:
Jan 26: no stop triggered anywhere, and every position acted well. GOOGL 333.26 (+1.6%, back above the whole Jan range, 26k sh normal volume) — the 318 trim line is far away. LIN 455.03, fourth straight up day and a new closing high on light volume; best low-beta trend I own. COST 977.67, small inside-day fade after 983 — no damage, 945 exit intact. META 672.36, third straight strong close, now above the Jan 2 662 level and the highest close of the month; my Jan 26 entry at 658.76 is working. GILD 137.78 on 10.0M sh, still extending from 121 — up ~14% in five sessions, so I will not add here, but nothing to sell. Semis mixed: MU 389.09 gave back 10 pts from 399 on lighter volume (29.2M vs 35.4M), AMAT 319.46 quietly flat with the tightest range in two weeks (322-316.57) — consolidation, not distribution; KLAC 1543 and STX 358 confirm the complex is still bid, so my reduced ~11% semi weight is fine.

No trades. Cash is only $6.0k (11%) and the $50k deposit lands Feb 2 (4 sessions), so the only thing $6k could buy is a starter at extension in names already running (GILD, META) or an add to GOOGL/COST which are 28%/25% weights. I'd rather deploy the deposit into bases.

Reconsider: MU<370 or AMAT<305 = out of that name. GOOGL<318 close = trim half; LIN<430 = out; COST<945 = exit; META<615 = out; GILD<126 = out. Feb 2 deposit: prioritise uncorrelated bases (healthcare/staples/software pullbacks), not chasing the semi or mega-cap extensions.

Jan 27: broad strength, no stop anywhere near. Semis re-accelerated — MU 410.24 (+5.4%) on 36.2M sh, a new closing high above the 399.65/412.43 Jan-23 marks, confirming the Jan-22 gap-and-reverse was a fakeout as I flagged; AMAT 332.71 (+4.1%) on 8.0M sh, best volume in two weeks and a clean break out of the 316-322 coil. My 40% MU trim at ~397 was early; I said I would not re-add above 410, and I will honour that — no chasing. GOOGL 334.55, quiet grind to new January closing high on lighter 21.6M sh. META 672.97, fourth firm close, flat-ish inside day = digestion not distribution. GILD 140.97 (+2.3%) on 10.6M, now +16% in six sessions, extended but strong; no add. LIN 453.03, first small down day after four up — trend fine above 430. COST 970.28 fading from 983 on falling volume; watch the 961 low, exit stays 945.

No trades. Cash $6.0k (11%) and the $50k deposit lands Feb 2 (3 sessions). Everything I own is at or near highs — nothing to buy at a sane entry with $6k, so I keep the powder for the deposit.

Reconsider: raise MU stop to a close <385 (locks most of the +39% gain); AMAT<310 = out. GOOGL<318 close = trim half; LIN<430 = out; COST<945 = exit; META<615 = out; GILD<126 = out. Feb 2 deposit: prioritise uncorrelated bases (healthcare, staples, software pullbacks) and do not add to GOOGL (28%) or COST (25%).

Jan 28: no stop hit. The intraday reversal is constructive but the volume signature after a 403->462 week is climactic churn, and my cost basis (464.76) is underwater. Everything made a new leg low on 2-3x volume: MSFT 381.87 (-1.8%, 50.9M vs ~26M normal), NVDA 172.70 (-3.3%, 241M), META 593.66 (under 600 for the first time this move), AAPL 247.99 on 88M, AMZN 205.37, AVGO 310.51, COST 972.33, WMT 119.02 (-1.7% on 57M - even the defensive bid is gone). - MU 422.90, low 415.36 - closes THROUGH my 435 stop. Sold the rest. Third straight 60M+ volume day after the 403->471 run; that is a distribution top, not a pullback.
- PANW 162.95 (-4.0%) on 16.46M, ~3x average, closed at the low and sliced the 167 shelf that had held for two weeks. Not at my 160 stop yet, but the breakdown is the signal, so I cut half rather than wait to be stopped at the number.

journal.text:
Mar 25 finally gave a qualifying signal, but not where I was looking. The index/mega-cap side is still broken: MSFT 371.04 (another new closing low, low 369.63), GOOGL 290.93 still under 296, META 594.89, PANW 153.22 (-2.5%, glad it's gone), CRWD 385.86 new low, DDOG 123.29. Nothing there to buy.

What changed is the semiconductor complex, on expanding volume and two consecutive higher closes:
- AMD 220.27 +7.3% on 48.5M, opened at its low and closed at the high, highest close since Feb 3 - clears the whole 200-210 range it has chopped in for six weeks.
- ARM 157.07 +16% on 29.6M, blowout to new highs (prior range high ~140).
- MRVL 98.45 +6.6% on 22.6M, clears the 93-95 March shelf.
- KLAC 1543 and AMAT 369 holding within 2% of new highs after strong Mar 23-24; LRCX 233 above its March range; ASML 1394 back at the top of its range; even INTC +7%.
- NVDA 178.68 +2.0% on 162M, first higher high in a week, still under my 180 line but acting better.

My written rule was "MSFT>395 AND NVDA>180" OR "two consecutive broad higher closes with semis leading on expanding volume." The breadth condition is only half-met, so I take a partial, group-concentrated position rather than a full one: $49k (~34% of net worth) into the semis, leaving ~$92k cash. No software, no mega-cap, no index proxy until MSFT stops making lower lows. Skipping ARM deliberately - a 16% single-day gap is a chase with too much overnight risk.

Stops (close-through): AMD <205; NVDA <172; MRVL <90; KLAC <1480; AMAT <352; PLTR <150 (kept, 154.96, still above).
If two of these five break within the same week, I go back to near-full cash - a failed group breakout in a tape of index lower lows is the definition of a bull trap. If instead MSFT reclaims 395 or the indexes put in two broad higher closes, I add a second tranche.

The semi breakout failed in a single session. Mar 26 was a textbook outside down day across the whole complex, on volume equal to or heavier than the breakout day:
- AMD 203.77 (-7.5%): opened 217.98, high 221, low 203.43, closed at the low on 49.2M. The entire Mar 25 range plus the breakout is gone; back inside the 200-210 chop.
- NVDA 171.24 (-4.2%) on 186M - closes THROUGH my 172 stop and below the Mar 20 low close.
- KLAC 1451 (-6.0%) through 1480; AMAT 338.55 (-8.3%) through 352, closed at the low; LRCX 211.62 (-9.4%); ASML 1329; MU 355.46 (-7%) still in freefall.
- MRVL 97.68: stop 90 not hit, but it also reversed from a 100.65 high to close red. It is the lone survivor of a failed group move, which is not a reason to hold it.
- PLTR 147.56 through 150.
- Tape-wide confirmation: MSFT 365.97 new closing low, GOOGL 280.92 slicing lower, META 547.54 (-8%) on 35.8M.

My written rule: if two of the five stops break in the same week, go back to near-full cash. Five broke on day one. Executing without negotiation - selling all six positions, back to ~100% cash (~$144k). The Mar 25 signal was a one-day bull trap in a tape of index lower lows; I paid ~$3-4k to find out, which is the intended cost of a partial-size probe.

Re-entry bar is now raised, not lowered: I need MSFT to stop making lower lows AND close >395, or two consecutive broad higher closes with semis leading where the second day HOLDS the prior day's range (the condition Mar 26 failed). Single-day surges no longer qualify; I've now been trapped by that pattern twice this month. Until then cash earns the right to wait, with April's deposit coming.

Mar 27 confirmed the risk-off tape a third time: MSFT 356.77 (another new closing low, -2.5%), NVDA 167.52 through 170, META 525.72, GOOGL 274.34, AMZN 199.34 (-3.9% closing at the low), AVGO 300.68, PLTR 143.06, CTAS 165.71, VRTX 433. No trace of a bottom in tech/mega-cap. My re-entry bar (MSFT >395 or two consecutive broad higher closes that HOLD the prior range) is nowhere close, so zero tech exposure stays right.

But the same tape shows a real rotation, not just liquidation: while the Nasdaq complex made new lows, COST 983.86 closed UP four of five sessions and at the high of its month; MDLZ 58.27 up five straight into new highs on rising volume; PEP 153.04 +1.5% off 150 support; AEP 130.10 +1.0% and back above its Mar 18 level; XEL 78.09 and LIN 491 both well off their Mar 20 lows; WMT 122.89 stable in the 121-124 band. Staples/utilities/defensive retail are absorbing the money leaving semis. That is a legitimate, low-beta way to be invested instead of sitting 100% cash indefinitely while $50k deposits keep arriving.

Action: $37.5k (~26% of net worth) split evenly across MDLZ, PEP, AEP, COST, WMT. Small, diversified, low-beta, no leverage to the AI trade. ~$106k cash retained for April's deposit and for a real tech re-entry signal.

Stops (close-through): MDLZ <56.0; PEP <149.0; AEP <125.5; COST <960; WMT <118.5. If two break in the same week, the rotation was a mirage and I go back to full cash. Tech re-entry still requires MSFT to stop making lower lows and close >395, or two consecutive broad higher closes with semis leading where day two holds day one's range.

Mar 30 confirmed the rotation for a second session while tech kept breaking: NVDA 165.17 (another new closing low, -1.4% on 186M), AMD 196.04 (-3%, low 192.87, gave back the whole Mar 27 bounce attempt), AVGO 293.41 (-2.4%, new low), MSFT 358.96 (weak bounce off 356 low, still far under 395), GOOGL 273.50 lower again, AMZN 200.95 and META 536.38 only dead-cat bounces inside big down days. Tech re-entry bar untouched; zero tech weight stays.

Meanwhile every defensive line I own made a new high on rising volume: PEP 156.82 (+2.5%, high 158.39, biggest volume in weeks - clean breakout from the 150-154 shelf), COST 996.58 (+1.3%, first close above 990), AEP 131.12, WMT 123.50, MDLZ 58.25 (only one digesting after five up days). Outside the book: XEL 79.17 new high, LIN 499.26 (+1.7%), EXC 49.11 (six straight up closes), KHC 22.34 (+1.4%, third strong day off 21). This is broad, persistent, volume-backed sector leadership, not a one-day pop - the pattern I was trapped by twice in semis looked nothing like this.

Action: second tranche of $30k into four NEW defensive names rather than chasing my extended winners - XEL, LIN, EXC, KHC at $7.5k each. Holdings go to ~$68k (~47% of net worth), cash ~$76k before April's deposit arrives. Still no leverage to the AI trade, eight positions, none above 6% of net worth.

Stops (close-through): XEL <75.5; LIN <478; EXC <46.5; KHC <21.0; existing MDLZ <56.0, PEP <149.0, AEP <125.5, COST <960, WMT <118.5. If three of nine break in one week I cut the whole basket back to cash. Tech re-entry unchanged: MSFT stops making lower lows and closes >395, or two consecutive broad higher closes with semis leading where day two holds day one's range.
